title: Target anatomy
view: Transverse section of the right lateral abdominal wall at the mid-axillary line, midway between the costal margin and the iliac crest, under a transverse probe, as on ultrasound: posterior on the image left, anterior on the right, skin at the top.
teachingPoint: The needle passes external and internal oblique; the tip sits in the plane between internal oblique and transversus abdominis, where the segmental nerves run, and the injectate opens that plane.
claims: Probe transverse at the mid-axillary line midway between the costal margin and the iliac crest (record).
External oblique, internal oblique and transversus abdominis over the peritoneum; the target is the plane between internal oblique and transversus (record).
Segmental nerve with a small artery in the plane, in its own sheath; transversalis fascia, preperitoneal fat, peritoneum and bowel deep (standard anatomy; house style for the sheath).
Needle in-plane from the anterior end, tip through the internal oblique fascia into the plane (record: anterior to posterior; pops through the internal oblique fascia).
Teal: spread opening the plane between internal oblique and transversus (record).
Labels: External oblique, Internal oblique, Transversus abdominis, TAP plane, Peritoneum.

geometry.why: internal oblique deep to external oblique
needle from the anterior end (anterior on the right)
needle enters beyond the probe's anterior end
spread below internal oblique, not between the obliques
